title: Traffic-surge-aware rollback triggering for model variants
creator: Julian Park
description: Goal: build a rollback trigger system that adapts SLO thresholds in real time for canary/A-B/shadow traffic based on traffic surge patterns, cohort baselines, and token-cost drift. Current problem: single static thresholds produce false positives during traffic bursts and false negatives for tiny but persistent regressions in high-cost tokens. This ticket implements a multi-signal scoring engine and a threshold tuner that distinguishes between transient load effects and true service regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New rollback signal computes a composite score from latency P95, error rate, token cost per request, and effective throughput. 2) System adjusts thresholds per cohort (region, customer tier, request size) using a 7-day baseline and flags deviations above configurable significance. 3) Traffic-surge detector temporarily raises tolerance and annotates the signal with surge metadata; normal rollback logic should be suppressed during identified upstream traffic spikes unless degradation persists past a configurable stabilization window. 4) End-to-end tests validate rollback decisions in simulation against labelled incidents (sensitivity >= 90% on injected regressions, FPR <= 5% on spike-only events). 5) Dashboard with signal breakdown and an RFC-ready doc describing tuning knobs exists. 6) Feature rollout behind a FF/flag and can be disabled instantly.
implementation_notes: Architecture: lightweight scoring service (stateless) that consumes per-route metrics from the metrics pipeline (Prometheus/OTLP aggregates) and emits time-series of composite scores to the rollout controller. Core components: 1) Cohort baseliner: computes rolling baselines for each cohort keyed by (route, region, plan, token_bucket). 2) Surge detector: compares inbound qps growth rate and queueing latency to detect upstream bursts. 3) Threshold tuner: Bayesian changepoint detector + empirical percentile adjustments to derive adaptive thresholds. 4) Decision policy: score -> verdict mapping with hysteresis windows and canary-traffic-aware decay. We will keep the scoring logic pluggable to iterate on weightings. Trade-offs considered: local (per-route) tuning vs global model — we start per-route with shared hyperparameters to limit configuration explosion. Use rate-limited writes to the rollout controller to avoid flapping. Keep failure modes fail-open (do not automatically rollback unless manual approval when signal confidence is low).
test_plan:
- Unit tests for scoring components and surge detector.
- Simulation harness: replay historical traffic traces with injected latency/error/token-cost anomalies.
- Chaos experiments in staging with canaries at 5/20/50% traffic and automated fault injection.
- A/B experiment comparing current static-threshold rollback vs adaptive system over 2 weeks, track false positives/negatives.
- Load test to verify scoring service handles 1k routes with 1s evaluation cadence per route.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated; enable scoring service in staging. 2) Run in 'shadow' mode for 72h (no action) and verify alerts and dashboard. 3) Enable advisory mode (controller can surface recommended rollback but requires manual confirmation) for a small group of internal canaries. 4) If metrics look good, enable automated decisioning for low-risk cohorts (internal, dev customers) with conservative thresholds. 5) Gradually expand to production cohorts after 2-week evaluation. 6) Keep global kill-switch and per-route overrides in Console.
